title: Timaeus
author: Plato (Jowett trans)
description: Timaeus by Plato, in the classic translation of Benjamin Jowett (Oxford, first edition 1871), with his introduction and analysis. Written around 360 BCE, the dialogue opens with Critias's tale of Atlantis and ancient Athens before Timaeus of Locri delivers a 'likely story' of cosmic creation. A good divine craftsman, the Demiurge, looking to eternal Forms, shapes the visible cosmos as a living being with a World Soul, made in the image of the eternal, with time as 'a moving image of eternity'. Timaeus describes the planetary circles, the receptacle or chora, the construction of the four elements from triangles corresponding to the regular solids, and the formation of the human body, soul, senses and diseases. The most influential Platonic dialogue in antiquity and the Middle Ages, it underlies Neoplatonism, Hermeticism, sacred geometry, Kepler's cosmology and the Atlantis legend.
